title: Ch-K-M

lines: THE ONE WHO CAN FIX ANYTHING.
THE ONE WHO KNOWS WHAT TO SAY.
cards: The person in your family who can fix anything. The aunt who knows exactly what to say at a funeral. The grandfather who rarely gives advice, but when he does, it lands.
None of them may have a degree in anything. English calls them handy, or tactful, or sharp. Hebrew can use one word for all three: chochmah, wisdom.
And the Torah uses it, strikingly, for a craftsman. Chet, kaf, mem: Ch-K-M. Wisdom with its sleeves rolled up.

teach.b: When the tabernacle is built in the wilderness, God says of the craftsman Bezalel, whom you met on day three hundred sixty-four, "I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship."
Wisdom lives in his hands: cutting stones, carving wood, working gold. A few chapters later, the women who spin for the tabernacle are called wise-hearted. Wisdom, in the Torah, can be a skill.
Second, the beginning. Proverbs, one of the Bible's books of wisdom, sets a starting line: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom."
Some readers hear fear as closer to awe: knowing you aren't the center of everything. Cleverness without awe isn't wisdom yet. Third, the learner.
In Pirkei Avot, the same Ben Zoma who asked who is honored asks: who is wise?
The one who learns from every person. Not the one with the most answers; the one with the most teachers. Fourth, the asking.

teach.h: THE ASKING: THE WISE ONE LISTENS.
teach.b: Proverbs puts it this way: the fool is sure his own way is right, while the wise one listens to advice.
Wisdom isn't only something you have. It's something you go and get, from someone else.
So chochmah looks less like a trophy on a shelf and more like a craft: practiced with your hands, rooted in awe, learned from anyone, and asked for out loud.

how: In Jewish life a learned scholar is called a talmid chacham, a student of the wise, and Jews often study Pirkei Avot, including Ben Zoma's teaching on who is wise, on Shabbat afternoons in the summer.

o: strength, the kind a warrior is praised for
patience, waiting calmly for the right moment
wisdom, including the skill in a maker's hands

p: the wise learn from every person

s: in the Torah, wisdom means only book learning
Bezalel is filled with wisdom for workmanship, and the women who spin are called wise-hearted.
in Pirkei Avot, the wise person is the one who learns from every person
Ben Zoma's answer to the question, who is wise?

games.q: the tabernacle needs building, and someone must be filled with wisdom for it. who?
o: a priest who knows the law.
games.why: Bezalel, filled "in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship."

practice: Think of a question you've been carrying alone: a decision, a worry, a conversation you don't know how to start.

Then think of someone whose judgment you trust, not necessarily the smartest person you know, but the one with chochmah in their hands or in how they listen, and shape the question in a sentence or two, the way you'd actually say it.
If you pray, you can ask for an understanding heart first.

wordCard.voice: Ch-K-M. Chet, kaf, mem: the root of chochmah, wisdom, and chacham, a wise person. In the Torah, it can be the skill of a craftsman's hands. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: wisdom; a wise person is a chacham.

carryVoice: Your line: wisdom. Sometimes it lives in a pair of hands. See you tomorrow, friend.
